chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yaqoob al-Kulayny said: He narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash’ari, from Al-Hussein ibn Ubaydullah, from Al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khishab, from Ali ibn Sama’at, from Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Rabat, from his father, from Ibn Aziat, from Zurarah ibn A’ayn who said: I heard Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) saying:

Twelve Imams from the Household of Muhammad (peace be upon them) are all Divinely Inspired (Muhaddathun) after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) is one of them.

key_terms.مُحَدَّثُونَ: Divinely Inspired (those who receive revelation without it being Quran)

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams and what is their status of divine inspiration after the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly identifies the twelve Imams as 'Muhaddathun' (those endowed with divine inspiration), linking their authority directly to the Prophet and Ali (AS). This narration serves as a foundational proof for the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing them as the sole legitimate successors in Shia theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-50 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yaqoob al-Kulayny quoted Abu Ali al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khishab, on the authority of Ali ibn Sama’at, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Rabat, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Aziat, on the authority of Zurarah ibn A’ayn that he had heard Aba Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) say,
“There are twelve Divine Leaders from the members of the Household of Muhammad (MGB) who all narrate traditions after God’s Prophet (MGB). Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) is one of them.”
